questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FM.1; MLA.A2.EX.4; MLA.A2.FN.2 (real-world application synthesis)

A phone plan charges $35 plus $12 per gigabyte. Which model gives monthly cost C for g gigabytes?

feedback.text: Correct. The fixed monthly charge is added to the variable data charge.
This reverses the fixed charge and the per-gigabyte rate.
This subtracts the fixed charge instead of adding it.
This is exponential, but the context has a constant rate per gigabyte.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FM.1; MLA.A2.EX.4; MLA.A2.FN.2 (real-world application synthesis)

A car loses 15% of its value each year from an initial value of $20,000. Which model fits the value after t years?

feedback.text: This is linear and does not model repeated percent decrease.
Correct. A 15% decrease leaves 85% of the value each year.
This represents a 15% increase, not depreciation.
This incorrectly uses the initial value as the exponential base.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FM.1; MLA.A2.EX.4; MLA.A2.FN.2 (real-world application synthesis)

A science model predicts h=3.4 meters for plant height. Which statement is most appropriate?

answer.text: The plant must be exactly 34 meters tall

feedback.text: This changes the scale of the prediction.

answer.text: The prediction is impossible because it is a decimal

feedback.text: Measurements can reasonably be decimals.

answer.text: The predicted height is 3.4 meters, subject to model assumptions

feedback.text: Correct. The value should be interpreted with units and assumptions.
Units are needed to make the answer meaningful.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FM.1; MLA.A2.EX.4; MLA.A2.FN.2 (real-world application synthesis)

Which data set is most likely to fit a linear model?

feedback.text: This pattern doubles, suggesting exponential growth.
This changes by a constant percent, suggesting exponential decay.
This has second differences that suggest a quadratic pattern.
Correct. The values increase by a constant difference of 3.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FM.1; MLA.A2.EX.4; MLA.A2.FN.2 (real-world application synthesis)

A table shows an account balance multiplied by about 1.04 each year. What does 1.04 represent?

feedback.text: Correct. Multiplying by 1.04 means the amount increases by 4% each year.
A factor greater than 1 indicates growth, not loss.
A multiplicative factor is not a fixed dollar increase.
The growth factor is separate from the initial value.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FM.1; MLA.A2.EX.4; MLA.A2.FN.2 (real-world application synthesis)

Which statement best explains why a model should be checked after solving?

feedback.text: Checking should preserve the original context.

answer.text: A solution may violate units, constraints, or reasonableness

feedback.text: Correct. Context determines whether the mathematical solution is usable.

answer.text: A correct equation never needs interpretation

feedback.text: Even correct equations need interpretation in context.

answer.text: Models are exact copies of reality

feedback.text: Models are simplified representations and must be evaluated.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FM.1; MLA.A2.EX.4; MLA.A2.FN.2 (real-world application synthesis)

A ticket model gives 18.1 tickets needed to break even. What minimum number of tickets should be sold?

feedback.text: Rounding down would not reach the break-even point.
A fractional ticket count is not possible.
Correct. The count must be a whole number and must meet the minimum.
This is not a whole number and overshoots unnecessarily.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FM.1; MLA.A2.EX.4; MLA.A2.FN.2 (real-world application synthesis)

Which situation is best modeled by a quadratic function?

answer.text: A bank account grows by 3% each year

feedback.text: Repeated percent growth is exponential.

answer.text: A taxi charges a starting fee plus a constant rate per mile

feedback.text: A fixed rate per mile is linear.
A constant difference is linear.

answer.text: The height of a thrown ball over time

feedback.text: Correct. Projectile height is commonly modeled by a quadratic function.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FM.1; MLA.A2.EX.4; MLA.A2.FN.2 (real-world application synthesis)

A scatterplot curves upward and ratios between y-values are nearly constant. Which model should be considered first?

feedback.text: Correct. Curved growth with near-constant ratios suggests an exponential model.
A linear model fits near-constant differences, not ratios.
The y-values are changing, so a constant model is not appropriate.
An absolute value model has a V-shape, not repeated ratio growth.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FM.1; MLA.A2.EX.4; MLA.A2.FN.2 (real-world application synthesis)

What does a residual represent in a data model?

feedback.text: A residual compares observed and predicted y-values.

answer.text: The difference between observed and predicted values

feedback.text: Correct. Residuals measure prediction error.
The starting value is a parameter, not a residual.
Residuals are values for individual predictions, not the count of data points.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FM.1; MLA.A2.EX.4; MLA.A2.FN.2 (real-world application synthesis)

Which interpretation is best if a model predicts a negative number of customers?

answer.text: Accept it because equations always give realistic answers

feedback.text: Equations can produce outputs outside a realistic context.
Customer counts cannot be negative.

answer.text: The model is not appropriate for that input or needs a domain restriction

feedback.text: Correct. The context requires a nonnegative count.

answer.text: Change customers to dollars without explanation

feedback.text: Changing units does not fix an invalid interpretation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FM.1; MLA.A2.EX.4; MLA.A2.FN.2 (real-world application synthesis)

A model has domain 0 <= t <= 12, where t is months after January. What does this domain mean?

feedback.text: The domain starts at 0, so negative values are excluded.

answer.text: The model only works for exactly 12 months

feedback.text: The interval includes all values from 0 through 12.

answer.text: The output must be between 0 and 12

feedback.text: The domain restricts input values, not output values.

answer.text: The model is intended for the first 12 months

feedback.text: Correct. The input t is limited to months 0 through 12.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FM.1; MLA.A2.EX.4; MLA.A2.FN.2 (real-world application synthesis)

A school wants at least $1,000. It already has $250 and earns $30 per sale. Which inequality models this goal?

feedback.text: Correct. Current funds plus sales revenue must be at least the goal.
This models staying at or below the goal.
This reverses the fixed amount and sale rate.
This does not represent the amount needed to reach the goal.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FM.1; MLA.A2.EX.4; MLA.A2.FN.2 (real-world application synthesis)

Which feature helps decide whether a regression model is useful?

feedback.text: Answer length does not measure model quality.
Correct. Residuals show how prediction errors behave.
Graph color does not determine fit.

answer.text: Whether the model has no variables

feedback.text: A useful model usually relates variables in context.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FM.1; MLA.A2.EX.4; MLA.A2.FN.2 (real-world application synthesis)

A model predicts revenue R=15x and cost C=200+5x. What equation finds the break-even point?

feedback.text: This ignores the variable cost of 5x.
This finds when cost is zero, not break-even.
Correct. Break-even occurs when revenue equals cost.
This does not match the revenue and cost expressions.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FM.1; MLA.A2.EX.4; MLA.A2.FN.2 (real-world application synthesis)

Which context would make a continuous model questionable?

feedback.text: Temperature can often be modeled continuously.
Water level can vary continuously.
Height can often be measured continuously.

answer.text: Number of individual raffle tickets sold

feedback.text: Correct. Ticket counts are discrete whole-number values.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FM.1; MLA.A2.EX.4; MLA.A2.FN.2 (real-world application synthesis)

If y=2x+9 models total cost in dollars, what does 9 most likely represent?

feedback.text: Correct. In a linear model, the y-intercept is the starting value.
The rate is the coefficient of x, which is 2.
Units sold are represented by x.

answer.text: The final answer for every input

feedback.text: The output changes as x changes.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FM.1; MLA.A2.EX.4; MLA.A2.FN.2 (real-world application synthesis)

Which is the best first step when building a model from a word problem?

feedback.text: Variables and relationships must be defined first.

answer.text: Identify quantities, units, and what the question asks

feedback.text: Correct. The model should begin from the context.

answer.text: Ignore the context and choose any equation

feedback.text: The equation must match the context.
Rounding too early can change the meaning of the problem.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FM.1; MLA.A2.EX.4; MLA.A2.FN.2 (real-world application synthesis)

Which model best represents a quantity that decreases by half each time period?

feedback.text: This adds a constant amount, so it is linear.
This does not repeatedly halve the quantity.
Correct. Multiplying by 0.5 each period gives repeated halving.
This is linear with a y-intercept of 0.5.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FM.1; MLA.A2.EX.4; MLA.A2.FN.2 (real-world application synthesis)

A student chooses an exponential model for data with a constant first difference. What is the likely issue?

answer.text: Constant first differences support exponential models

feedback.text: Constant first differences usually indicate linear behavior.
A constant first difference supports a linear model, not necessarily quadratic.
Differences are useful for comparing model types.

answer.text: A linear model would likely be more appropriate

feedback.text: Correct. Constant differences are a key signal for linear modeling.
